Almost every laptop first thing disable everything thru msconfig, buy Win 7 Pro if possible, then 8.1 if I must (again pro if possible)... NEVER 10.

Best bet is to do a wipe and install of Win 7 Pro with keycode, 8.1 is bit harder. You can order install software from most places or create your own when setting up the laptop.... speaking of setting it up, with 8.1 do not connect to the internet during setup and create a "local" account. Do not create an account with an email address and password, all "apps" on the app side (the dark side) will be connected automatically to the internet as soon as you log onto the laptop, not when you access the internet thru a browser.

When updating make sure "recommended updates" is unchecked, nothing but crap nowadays.

So recommendation is buy in your price range, clean the crap out of it, enjoy. If it comes with 4GB (at least) make sure you can upgrade to at least 8 and buy it later for not much. Stephen Harper attempted to thrust partisanship on to the public service and was roundly, and deservedly, criticized for doing so. It supports the notion that Conservative distrust of the establishment was reasonable.
